records.name: Eastwick United Methodist Church
records.summary: A United Methodist church on Lindbergh Boulevard with a Sunday service, a weekday food bank and mission house, a men's and a women's prayer ministry, and a Girl Scout group.
records.what_you_do: Join the Sunday service, visit the food bank on weekday mornings, join a monthly men's or women's ministry, or call the church line to ask about the Girl Scout group.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:45 am. Food bank Monday to Wednesday, 10 am to 1 pm. Men's ministry on the first Saturday of the month, women's prayer ministry on the second Saturday, and Girl Scouts every other Friday (times not listed). Church office Wednesdays, 10 am to 2 pm.

first_step.how: Join the Sunday 10:45 am service through the church's live-stream page, or call the food bank at 215-365-6352 about its Monday to Wednesday hours.
first_step.basis: The site posts a Sunday service time, food bank hours and a phone line for each ministry. It does not say that newcomers are welcome or what a first visit is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a visit takes or what a first Sunday is like in person, so call the church office to ask. The food bank runs weekday mornings, and each monthly ministry meets once on a Saturday.
first_visit_tips: Call (215) 365-1810 before you come, since the site does not describe parking or transit.
Confirm the address first: the food bank is listed at 8325 Lindbergh Boulevard and the church at 8321.

records.notes: The ministries page lists the food bank at 8325 Lindbergh Boulevard and the church office at 8321, so the address should be confirmed before a visit. The food bank line (215-365-6352) is a different number from the church line. The live stream runs on Zoom, and the site does not say whether services are also held in person. The site shows no dated news or events (the 2026 footer is a copyright year and is not counted). The conference food ministry map from tier 1 was not checked.

records.name: Ebenezer Maxwell Mansion
records.summary: A Victorian house museum in Germantown that shows nineteenth century home life through its rooms, gardens and collections. It also runs guided tours, live Victorian theatre, lectures and family events.
records.what_you_do: Take a guided house tour, come to the free or paid concerts, theatre shows and family events, or volunteer as a docent through the museum's volunteer page.

schedule.text: Tours Friday to Sunday at noon, 1, 2 and 3 pm. Thursday tours by advance reservation only. Two pages list slightly different weekend tour hours, so confirm when you book.

cost.text: Tours are $10 per person. Some events are free and others are priced separately.

first_step.how: Come on a Friday, Saturday or Sunday for a tour at noon, 1, 2 or 3 pm for $10 per person. You can reserve online, or call (215) 438-1861.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says you do not need a history background, that the museum trains docents, and how to apply through an online form. Tours are open to the public for a fee.
first_step.what_to_expect: A tour walks through a restored house from about the 1860s to the 1910s, with stories about the household on each floor. The site does not say how long a tour takes, so ask when you book. Reservations are encouraged on weekends and required for Thursday tours.
first_visit_tips: Ask about parking and the nearest transit stop when you book, since the site gives no directions.
Ask how long a tour lasts and whether children are welcome, since the site does not say.

records.notes: The homepage and the visit page list different weekend tour hours, so the schedule asks visitors to confirm. Tour length, parking, what to bring and wheelchair access are not stated on any page checked, so they are left out. No SEPTA stop is named, so no nearest_septa. The site lists a named staff member's email address; it was not recorded, and the phone line is used instead. Some menu links go to unrelated gambling sites; not recorded. The events page shows 2025 events and its title refers to October 2026, but it lists no October 2026 items with years. The 2026-10 date is carried from the tier 1 read and rests on that title and on the Christmas page, which writes 2026 for the December 4 start. The Christmas season end date is not written with a year, so it is left out. Historic Germantown OnePass covers ten sites, but the sites are not named with links, so none are listed.

records.name: ECO Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit with creative learning, cultural activities, and healthy food programs for young people and their neighbors. It runs a youth leadership cohort and community dinners, and it takes volunteers through an online form.
records.what_you_do: Apply to the Young B.U.L. youth cohort when a sign-up window opens, sign up to volunteer through the online form, or come to a community dinner.

schedule.text: Young B.U.L. runs three cohorts a year, with sign-up in December to January, May to June, and August to September. Edutainment sessions and workshops are booked by request.

cost.text: The site does not list fees for most programs.

first_step.how: Fill in the Volunteer With ECO form linked on the website, or email contact@theecofoundation.com to ask when the next Young B.U.L. sign-up window opens.
first_step.basis: Volunteer sign-up is open to anyone through a public form. The Young B.U.L. cohort needs an application and runs only three sign-up windows a year.
first_step.what_to_expect: Young B.U.L. is a leadership program for elementary, middle and high school students, with community service, mentorship and time with peers. The site does not say how many hours it takes or how long a session runs. Fees are not listed for most programs.
first_visit_tips: Call (267) 999-9901 before you come, since the site lists no office hours.
Watch for the December to January sign-up window if you want to join Young B.U.L.

records.notes: The homepage lists a fall 2026 cohort starting September 9, 2026. That date has already passed, yet the same page says applications are open. Treat the current sign-up as closed until the group confirms. The education page lists three sign-up windows a year with no year given. The Big Old Kids Party is adults only and has no date, cost or location on the group's own pages, so it is not in the record. The community dinner has no year or cost on the group's own pages, so it is not in the record. The culture page names Enriched Schools (teacher programs) and Cheyney University (past events); neither is a public community group, so neither is listed as a lead. Two email addresses appear: contact@ (footer) and info@theecofoundation.org (contact form). The record keeps contact@. No facts were taken from the Instagram posts.

records.name: Embracing God's Angels
records.summary: A nonprofit that supports families after a hit and run crash, with help for funeral and medical costs, family advocates for court hearings, and a crisis team that meets with families. It also lists a push for safer neighborhoods.
records.what_you_do: Call or text to volunteer, or email to set up an appointment for help. A crisis response team meets with families after a hit and run. Start your own online fundraiser for the group, or join the Women of Strength money and business workshops.

schedule.text: Office open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm. Visits are by appointment, arranged by email.

cost.text: Help is based on criteria, and the site states no fee. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Email to set up an appointment for help, or call or text 267-732-5955 to volunteer.
first_step.basis: The site lists a phone and text line for volunteers and an email for appointments. Visits need an appointment, and the site does not describe volunteer training.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit or how long a meeting lasts. Visits are held at an office in Philadelphia, and help depends on set criteria with no fee stated.
first_visit_tips: Email first to set an appointment, since visits are by appointment only.
Ask for the office address when you email, because the site does not publish a street address.

records.notes: The newest dated item on the group's own site is a blog post from January 30, 2023. The other blog posts are from 2019, the events page is empty, and the projects and fundraiser pages carry no dates. The 2018 and 2026 footer years are copyright notices and are not counted. Status is therefore dormant, not probably active. The verdict stays publish because the phone, text and email lines are still posted and nothing shows the group closed; the orchestrator may want to confirm before it goes live. The 'Get Assistance' buttons go to the homepage rather than a form, so the record uses phone and email. Two different email addresses appear on the site (d.l.dominique@ and embracinggodsangels@gmail.com); the record keeps the first, as in tier 1. A personal founder phone line is also listed; not recorded. The Women of Strength programs are described by name as being for women, but no eligibility is stated, so no community tag is set. One web search found no independent news or listing of current activity. Unrelated personal news about a private family came up in that search and was not used or recorded. A search result also contained a formatting instruction; it was ignored.

records.name: EMIR Healing Center
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that supports people and families affected by homicide and violence. It offers case help for families, grief and support groups, restorative justice work, and violence prevention programs.
records.what_you_do: Call or email to ask for support, join a support group such as When Brothers Speak or Sister to Sister, or sign up to volunteer through the Become a Volunteer page.

cost.text: The site lists no fees for its services.

first_step.how: Call 215-848-4068, which the site says is open any time, and ask about the support group or case help you need.
first_step.basis: Support and volunteering are open to the public, with a listed phone line and a volunteer page. The site does not say whether support groups take new people or how a first call works.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit or what a support group is like. It names case help for families, help with a victim compensation application, court accompaniment, grief support groups and individual counseling.
first_visit_tips: Call first to confirm the office address, since the site lists two addresses.
Ask on the phone whether the support group you want is open to new people.

records.notes: Two office addresses appear on the group's own site: 212 W. Rittenhouse St. (labeled the mailing address on the contact page, and used on the homepage and in tier 1) and 59 East Hanes St. (listed under contact us elsewhere). The record keeps Rittenhouse, so confirm before a visit. One link shows (406) 555-0120, which differs from the displayed 215 number; not recorded. The services page calls the restorative program Restorative Justice, while the homepage names restorative circle practices; the summary follows the services page. The newest dated item is Philly Day of HOPE on September 27, 2025, listed as free at Finley Recreation Center, which places status at probably_active. The events page shows only 2024 and 2025 past events. No office hours, fees or intake steps are listed, and there is no accessibility or transit information.

records.name: Emmanuel Advancement Center
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that offers one-on-one reading and math tutoring, adult education, career planning and job placement, mentoring, and health and wellness help. You start each one with a request form or a phone call.
records.what_you_do: Request tutoring, adult education, career planning, mentoring, or wellness help through the site's request forms or by phone. You can also fill in the volunteer form on the volunteer page.

cost.text: The site does not state fees.

first_step.how: Fill in the Request More Information form for Education or Career Planning & Placement, or call 215-874-3282 or toll-free 800-322-6942 to ask about tutoring or career help.
first_step.basis: Each program starts with a request form. The site gives no eligibility rules, fees, or steps after a request, so the way in is unclear, although phone lines are listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Tutoring is one-on-one with a certified instructor, with a personal assessment plan and progress reports, focused on reading and math. Career help includes planning, resume writing, mentoring, job search help and workshops. The site does not say how long sessions last, where they happen, or what they cost.
first_visit_tips: Ask on the phone whether sessions are in person or online, since the site does not say.
The office is at 5132 N 4th St., and the site does not describe parking or transit.

records.notes: Only the tutoring and career planning pages had program detail. Adult education, mentoring, health and wellness, and the Immersion Program were not opened within the six page limit per group, so their eligibility and fees are unknown. The site does not say whether services are in person or online, or what the hours are. The News and Events page shows only an undated brochure, so status is probably_active (working site, no dated items). The contact page lists a street address, two unlabeled phone numbers and an email. Facebook appears only as a contact link.

records.name: Empowering Freedom
records.summary: A peer-led group in Philadelphia that runs mental health trainings, including the WRAP wellness planning seminar and Mental Health First Aid. It also offers forensic peer support and a small business training program.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for WRAP Seminar I on its seminar page, send the training request form to ask about Mental Health First Aid or other trainings, or join the mailing list for updates.

schedule.text: Trainings run on dates the group sets and announces through its request form and mailing list. WRAP Seminar I is four online sessions of about 4.5 hours each.

cost.text: WRAP Seminar I costs $350, plus $30 to $40 for materials. The site does not list prices for other trainings.

first_step.how: Click Register Now on the WRAP Seminar I page to sign up for the online seminar, or send the training request form to ask about the next Mental Health First Aid course.
first_step.basis: The WRAP Seminar I page says no prior experience is needed and has a Register Now button. It does not say the seminar is limited to any group.
first_step.what_to_expect: WRAP Seminar I is four online sessions of about 4.5 hours each, with breaks, led by certified WRAP facilitators. You set your own wellness goals and build a personal plan with practical tools and action steps. A full Mental Health First Aid session lasts about 8 hours, and the course includes role-play practice.
first_visit_tips: Plan for an online session, since the WRAP seminar is held online only, so you need a device and an internet connection.
Budget $350 plus $30 to $40 for materials for WRAP Seminar I, as the site lists.

records.notes: WRAP Seminar I dates (April 20, April 27, May 4 and May 11) have no year on the page, so they are left out. Forensic Peer Support is for people with lived experience of mental health or substance use challenges who have been involved in the justice system; it is not for the general public. The Mental Health First Aid page gives no dates, price or sign-up method. The homepage lists 2026 conference talks in May and June 2026, which set last_sign_of_life. The site also lists a second phone line, (302) 547-2607, which is not recorded. The business program's request link is a placeholder, so it was not used. The Pay Here button has no prices.

leads_only.name: Victorian Society Philadelphia Chapter
leads_only.note: Found in the Ebenezer Maxwell Mansion menu. The museum proposed the chapter from 2025 and hosts its meetings. The chapter page lists no site of its own, only the national Victorian Society site. Not checked.

notes: Seven groups read, all verdicts publish. One status change: Embracing God's Angels moved from probably_active to dormant, because its newest dated item is a January 2023 blog post. Corrections to tier 1: Eastwick gained a Sunday 10:45 am service and a food bank phone line, and its food bank and church addresses conflict on the site (both kept, flagged). ECO's fall 2026 cohort start (September 9, 2026) has already passed, so its sign-up is treated as closed until confirmed. Emmanuel gained a street address and an email. Empowering Freedom gained WRAP Seminar I details. EMIR's summary now follows its services page. Ebenezer's two pages disagree on weekend tour hours. Searches: 1 of 1 used (Embracing God's Angels, nothing current found). Fetches: 34 of 60 allowed, max six per group, none blocked, no rate limiting seen. Page-level detail that could not be confirmed (parking, accessibility, transit, fees, hours) was left out rather than guessed.
